title_en: Chen Yangshan: Hero of the Secret War
publisher: CCP Party History Press (Zhonggong Dangshi Chubanshe)
description: Chen Yangshan (1906–1991) was one of the Chinese Communist Party’s most secretive professional revolutionaries and a leading figure on its ‘hidden front’ of intelligence and security work. Drawn into the underground in the 1920s, he helped Zhou Enlai build the Party’s first intelligence apparatus—the Central Special Branch—ran agents through the war against Japan and the civil war, and rose to senior posts in the new People’s Republic, only to be purged in 1958 and rehabilitated decades later. Drawing on archives and the recollections of his old comrades, Yao Huafei reconstructs the life of a man who spent it in the shadows, content to be a nameless hero.
rights: English translation prepared for private study. Original text © Yao Huafei and CCP Party History Press.
source_ref: 秘战英雄陈养山, 中共党史出版社 (Beijing), 2018. ISBN 978-7-5098-4587-5.
publisher_series_zh: 隐蔽战线春秋书系·传记卷
publisher_series_en: The Hidden Front Chronicles — Biography Volume
translator_note: This is an English translation of 秘战英雄陈养山 (Chen Yangshan: Hero of the Secret War) by Yao Huafei, published by the CCP Party History Press in 2018 as a biography volume in the Hidden Front Chronicles series. The source was an image-only scan with no digital text layer; the Chinese was recovered by optical character recognition and verified against the page images.

Chen Yangshan worked for most of his life in secret, and the book is a Party biography written to honour him: it is candid about his persecution but frames his career in the celebratory register of its genre. Where the account is self-serving, contested by other sources, or silent on what an outside historian would ask, the footnotes say so. Names of people, places and organisations follow standard pinyin except where an English form is long established; every rendering is fixed once in the glossary. Passages the scan left doubtful, and claims that scholarship corroborates, contradicts, or cannot confirm, are flagged in the notes.
source_note: Image-only PDF scan (DuXiu/SuperStar digitisation via Anna’s Archive), 243 PDF pages; 231 printed book pages plus front matter and an appended metadata leaf (PDF p243, not book content). No text layer. Modern simplified Chinese, single column, horizontal. Clean typeface—OCR is straightforward. Chapter-opener rectos carry a photograph above the heading; a frontispiece portrait sits at PDF p5 and the colour cover at p1.
toc_flags_open: Printed TOC lists back matter through the Afterword; verified all openers against the scan. Appendix has three parts (生平 214 / 遗作 217 / 年谱 223), then References (228) and Afterword (230). The series foreword (丛书前言, Zhang Baijia) sits at PDF 7-8 on its own folio sequence and is NOT in the printed TOC.
